messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime p95/p99 regression detected for /v1/generate (hosted / us-west-2). p95 jumped ~2x, p99 ~2.5x over last 5m. Streaming stalls +15%. Triggering page to oncall_sre. link: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/abc123/latency?orgId=1 :rotating_light:

oncall_sre: i'm up — looking at traces + logs. grabbing perf dashboard and traces now :eyes:

maria: runtime dashboard shows concurrency queue spike on inference-pool-5, CPU and socket wait high on 3 pods. spike begins ~22:10 UTC. correlated with rollout tag: adaptive-batch-v2.

alice: ran a synthetic streaming request to the hosted endpoint, here's the curl and output showing chunk pauses (~700ms gaps):
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?stream=true\" -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
```
```
> GET /v1/generate 200
chunk 1 (0.12s)
chunk 2 (0.13s)
chunk 3 (0.82s)  <-- big gap
chunk 4 (0.11s)
```

bob: pulling model-serving metrics — kvcache hit-rate dropped from ~94% to ~66% at the same time as rollout. My hypothesis: new batching heuristic changed key access patterns and broke prefetch.

raj: any immediate customer impact? carla, do we have errors reported?

carla: support summary: 3 paying customers show elevated error rates (timeouts) in last 10m. one enterprise tenant (cust-zenith) seeing 2% request failures; flagged P1 by CS. notifying them now with interim note.

oncall_sre: quick triage checklist (doing in parallel):
1) confirm rollout impact (maria + bob)
2) toggle adaptive-batch-v2 flag to off (feature-flag service)
3) scale inference-pool-5 by +2 replicas
4) enable degraded routing for high-tier customers to fallback quantized model variant
5) start KV prefetch/warming job
6) keep customers updated (carla)

maria: confirming rollout was a global canary at 22:05 then ramped to 50% at 22:10. timing lines up.

oncall_sre: executing mitigation 1 & 2 now. tagging @alice to run the flag change and @raj to execute scale if needed.

alice: disabling flag via feature service...
```bash
curl -X POST https://flags.redwood.ai/api/v1/flags/adaptive-batch-v2 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"enabled":false}'
```
response: 200 OK. Disabled. :white_check_mark:

alice: immediate effect visible — p95 dropped from ~1.2s to ~0.58s in the next 30s on the canary dashboard. p99 trending down but not fully recovered yet. link: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/abc123/latency?from=now-15m

raj: scaling inference-pool-5 replicas +2 to give breathing room
```bash
kubectl -n prod scale deploy/inference-pool-5 --replicas=12
```
kubectl output: scaled. pods coming up.

bob: kicked off KV prefetch job to re-warm caches for the active keys. hit-rate now trending up: 66% -> 78% in 2m. streaming stalls decreasing on canary.

incident-bot: Updated metrics: p95 back to ~0.6s, p99 ~1.1s (still above target but improving). streaming stall rate down to +4% vs baseline.

carla: sent interim customer messages to the 3 affected customers. included mitigations and ETA for full recovery. No escalations expected yet.

alice: routing-service temporary rule created to route cust-zenith to quantized-variant-v1 for critical requests. command: POST to /routing/overrides.

raj: monitoring logs — one inference node shows repeated "KV-MISS: prefetch_timeout" entries around 22:10. probable root cause: prefetch worker crashed during rollout due to race with new batching.

maria: putting a quick note on the incident board: suspected cause = adaptive-batch-v2 change -> key access skew -> prefetch worker gap -> KV miss spike -> tail latency.

oncall_sre: current severity: P1 (customer-impacting). Mitigations applied. Next: continue monitoring, let KV warming settle, roll back canary to stable by default. assign postmortem to eng-runtime + eng-ml to investigate prefetch logic and batching interactions.

bob: saving logs and trace snapshot for postmortem. will include flamegraphs from the affected pods.

carla: updating customer notes: next update in 20m or on recovery.

oncall_sre: handoff timeline — i'm on call for another 45m, then raj will be primary. tagging @pagerduty for formal handoff.

pagerduty: Acknowledged. Next oncall: raj. Please include summary in incident ticket and create follow-up tasks.

alice: quick follow-up: p95 now stable at ~0.55s on prod, p99 at ~0.9s. continuing to watch for ~15m before closing the paging.

maria: adding action items: (1) revert adaptive-batch-v2 rollout until tested with KV warmers (2) harden prefetch worker restart logic (3) add automated alarms for kvcache hit-rate drop threshold (4) add canary runbook step to validate key-hit curves before ramp.

oncall_sre: thanks team. keeping this thread open for final confirmation and postmortem assignment. :thumbsup:
